KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 (Reuters) - Southeast Asian foreign ministers will discuss how to tackle haze blanketing parts of the ​region ahead of the ASEAN bloc's summit next ‌month, Malaysia's top diplomat said on Monday.

* Forest and land fires that have raged for months in Indonesia have in recent weeks ​caused thick haze in Singapore and in Malaysia, ​which closed schools in several states last week after ⁠air pollution levels hit unhealthy levels
* The wildfires, mainly on ​the islands of Sumatra and Borneo, are Indonesia's most ​intense in 11 years
* While the Association of Southeast Asian Nations has existing mechanisms to deal with natural disasters such as floods ​or volcano eruptions, haze is not included in ​those, Malaysian Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan told reporters
* "So this is one ‌of ⁠the issues that I will personally bring in a meeting with my counterparts, ahead of the 49th summit in Manila next month," he said, according to his ​office
* ASEAN chair ​the Philippines ⁠did not immediately respond to a request for confirmation that the haze issue would ​be on the agenda
* Malaysia has previously offered assistance ​to ⁠Indonesia to combat fires
* Fire-fighting attempts in many areas were complicated by poor visibility, accessibility issues and a lack ⁠of suitable ​conditions for cloud seeding, Mohamad ​said, citing discussions with Indonesia's foreign minister

Reporting by Rozanna Latiff; Additional reporting ​by Mikhail Flores in Manila; Editing by Martin Petty
